name: SignNow
summary: Electronic signatures and custom eSignature workflows by airSlate. Send, sign and manage documents on any device — legally binding and team-friendly.
best_for: teams where many people sign occasionally and want unlimited users on one plan - size it against the 100 invites a year, not the headcount
skip_if: you need the deepest enterprise integrations and workflows: that's where the incumbent still earns its premium
honest_knock: It's built for straightforward everyday signing, if you need deep contract-lifecycle (CLM) features, a heavier platform fits better.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: Three plans on signNow's live checkout page, read in a browser on 26 September 2026 from the EU: Business EUR 8, Business Premium EUR 15 and Enterprise EUR 30 a month billed annually, against EUR 20, EUR 30 and EUR 50 month-to-month (the cards state the annual saving as EUR 144, EUR 180 and EUR 240); signnow.com/pricing.md, read the same day, gives the annual rates as $8, $15 and $30 per user a month. Every card says 'Unlimited users' and 'Get 100 invites per year': the FAQ puts annual plans at up to 100 signature invites per account per year and monthly plans at up to 10 a month, after which the plan moves to pay-as-you-go for the extra invites, at a rate the page does not state. A Site License is billed at $1.50 per signature invite instead, with custom invite volumes, aimed at organisations sending 1,000+ documents a year, and is where SSO, full API access and phone support appear; HIPAA, 21 CFR Part 11 and QES are add-ons on top. airSlate Business Cloud is $50 per user a month and bundles signNow with airSlate, pdfFiller and US Legal Forms. Free 7-day trial, no credit card required; refunds can be requested within 30 days of the invoice.

measured.comparability: SignNow: Only Site License at 1000 invites; no claim about Business invite overages or an equivalent historical volume.
measured.buying_consequence: The observed per-invite rate is higher than the dossier figure.

exit_test.what: Uploaded attachment-AIBM-001.pdf at about 14:20 UTC. Closed the recipient dialog without adding a recipient. The document was stored in My Documents. AIBM-002 and custom/text fields were not entered. Business Premium defaulted to yearly and 1 seat; setting 25 seats kept $240/year. Business with 25 seats was $96/year, or $20 monthly. Seats were described as free. No invite limit or overage was visible for Business/Premium: invite 101 remains unpriced by this test. Site License at 1000 invites showed $1.75 each, total $1750. SSO listed Entra ID, Google Cloud Identity, Okta, OneLogin and SAML; Add SSO Configuration opened an upgrade window with Business Premium selected. The exact tier unlocking SSO was not established.
exit_test.awkward: Invite 101 cost was not disclosed in Business/Premium checkout; SSO entitlement tier remained unclear.

sessions.what: We started a signNow free trial on 12 November 2026 and read the checkout for three plans. We uploaded one test PDF, but did not add a recipient, fields or a signature, and did not download or re-import anything. We stopped before paying.
findings: The trial started without a card: 'No credit card required' sat under the e-mail field and the app opened without payment details. A banner said 'Upgrade Plan: 7 Days Left'.
Business Premium was preselected, billed annually, 1 seat, '$240 x 1 year'. At 25 seats the price stayed '$240 x 1 year', beside the text 'User seats are free. Add as many as you need.'

Business at 25 seats showed '$96 x 1 year' (annual) and '$20 x 1 month' (monthly). That is a price per account, not per user. Our earlier page said '$8 per user a month billed annually', which this checkout contradicts.
The Business and Business Premium checkout showed no invitation limit and no price for extra invitations, so what invitation 101 costs is not shown there.
Site License with 1000 documents a year showed '$1.75 per invite' and '$1.75 x 1000 invites, $1750'. Our earlier page said $1.50 per invite.
Single Sign-on is listed under Admin Settings. Clicking 'Add SSO Configuration' during the trial opened the upgrade window with Business Premium selected; it did not say which plan unlocks SSO.
No tax line was visible. Payment options were PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay and card.
not_tested: Adding recipients and fields, and sending a document for signature
Export and re-import (a Download option is in the document menu)
Support, invitations, roles beyond the menu entry, and API access
Downgrade, cancellation, tax and the final price
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

open_questions.question: Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?

Our price check could not put a number on this part of the cost: Signature invites beyond 100 a year (annual) or 10 a month (monthly) are pay-as-you-go at a rate the page does not state. Can you publish the price or the rule?
